messages.subject: Re: Can blavan handle categorical data?
messages.body_plain:
> When you say that Blavaan does not currently support categorical variables, does this include exogenous covariates as well?

No, there are no distributional assumptions about exogenous variables, so it is arbitrary whether they are continuous or discrete.  For proper interpretation, it is up to you to include dummy codes that make sense.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: BIC computation
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dr. Merkle,

I tried to compute and verify the BIC using the loglikelihood reported from the Blavaan output. However, my computation using the BIC formula (BIC = -2 * loglikelihood + d * log(N)) did not match the BIC reported from Blavaan. It seems that the BIC reported using a sample size that doubles the number of observations in my simulated dataset (continuous data). I used the following code with the developmental version of Blavaan:

model <- 'f =~ NA*x1+x2+x3+x4+x5+x6+x7+x8+x9+x10+x11+x12
                f~~1*f'
run1 <- bcfa(model, data = dat, group = "grp", convergence = "auto", n.chains = 2, bcontrol = list(method = "rjparallel"))
fit1 <- fitmeasures(run1)

Here is a sample output (n=75):

  npar1     logl1    ppp1     bic1     dic1   p_dic1    waic1  p_waic1     loo1   p_loo1    mlogl1
1    72 -2267.698 0.49825 4895.195 4676.975 70.78994 4681.485 71.05709 4682.442 71.53554 -2576.311
2    72 -2231.714 0.78860 4823.227 4604.780 70.67646 4606.002 68.55050 4607.004 69.05152 -2544.540

Could you help explain how the BIC is computed in Blavaan? Thank you so much for your time!

Xinya

messages.subject: Re: BIC computation
messages.body_plain:
Xinya,

It should be the usual BIC computation. When you say "doubles the number of observations", do you possibly mean "parameters" instead of "observations? If so, then this may come from the group argument. That is, if you have two groups, then you will have twice as many free parameters as you would with one group.

If that's not it, then I'm not sure where your sample output is coming from. I don't think any blavaan commands would give you two rows like that. What is the difference between rows 1 and 2?

Finally, instead of manually fixing the latent variance to 1 in the model syntax, please use the argument std.lv <http://std.lv>=TRUE. This will help the chains converge.

Ed

messages.subject: mcmcextra and latent interactions
messages.body_plain:
Hey all,
I am trying to create a nonlinear interaction via mcmcextra, but I can't get mcmcextra to work for very simple cases. I am sure I am using it incorrectly.
Let me start by saying that if there is an easier way to use blavaan for nonlinear SEM, please let me know. I am trying to find the simplest way to do this for a large simulation study.

Here is a simple reproducible example of when I get my error. Here I am trying to have JAGS function as if the model syntax was the same as sim.mod. The ultimate goal is to be able to include the interaction via mcmcextra.

The error says:

 " RUNTIME ERROR:
Compilation error on line 96.
Index out of range taking subset of..."

And the variable that is problematic changes depending on order.
I think the code should work, it is exported with mcmcfile = T from a model specified as eta =~ Y1+ Y2 + Y3. I did have to change the subscripts, but I am pretty sure they are correct despite the error. I would be glad to admit that I am wrong on that though.

library(lavaan)
library(blavaan)

sim.mod <-
  'xi1 =~ X1 + X2 + X3
   xi2 =~ X4 + X5 + X6
   eta =~ Y1 + Y2 + Y3
'
data = data.frame(simulateData(sim.mod, sample.nobs = 100))

model <-
  'xi1 =~ X1 + X2 + X3
   xi2 =~ X4 + X5 + X6
'

  blin <- bsem(model, data=data,
bcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"),
mcmcextra = list(syntax='
    for(i in 1:N) {
    Y1[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i,7], 1/theta[7,7,g[i]])
    Y2[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i,8], 1/theta[8,8,g[i]])
    Y3[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i,9], 1/theta[9,9,g[i]])
    mu[i,7] <- nu[7,1,g[i]] + lambda[7,3,g[i]]*eta[i,3]
    mu[i,8] <- nu[8,1,g[i]] + lambda[8,3,g[i]]*eta[i,3]
    mu[i,9] <- nu[9,1,g[i]] + lambda[9,3,g[i]]*eta[i,3]
    lambda[7,3,1] <- 1
    lambda[8,3,1] <- parvec[17]
    lambda[9,3,1] <- parvec[18]
    eta[i,3] ~ dnorm(mu_eta[i,3], 1/psi[3,3,g[i]])
    mu_eta[i,3] <- alpha[3,1,g[i]] + beta[3,1,g[i]]*eta[i,1] + beta[3,2,g[i]]*eta[i,2]
  }
  beta[3,1,1] <- parvec[19]
  beta[3,2,1] <- parvec[20]
  psi[3,3,1] <- pow(parvec[21],-1)
  parvec[19] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
  parvec[20] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
  parvec[21] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
  theta[7,7,1] <- pow(parvec[22],-1)
  theta[8,8,1] <- pow(parvec[23],-1)
  theta[9,9,1] <- pow(parvec[24],-1)
  nu[7,1,1] <- parvec[25]
  nu[8,1,1] <- parvec[26]
  nu[9,1,1] <- parvec[27]
  alpha[3,1,1] <- 0
  psi[3,3,1] <- bpsi[3,3,1]
  psi[1,3,1] <- bpsi[1,3,1]
  psi[2,3,1] <- bpsi[2,3,1]
  parvec[17] ~ dnorm(0,1e-2)
  parvec[18] ~ dnorm(0,1e-2)
  parvec[22] ~ dgamma(1,.5)
  parvec[23] ~ dgamma(1,.5)
  parvec[24] ~ dgamma(1,.5)
  parvec[25] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
  parvec[26] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
  parvec[27] ~ dnorm(0,1e-3)
'))

messages.subject: Re: mcmcextra and latent interactions
messages.body_plain:
Isaac,

This is a good attempt! I have not tried the code, but I think I see one issue. When the model syntax only involves X1-X6 (and not Y1-Y3), then the only data that gets passed to jags is X1-X6, even if Y1-Y3 is in the original data frame.

I think I need to add a "data" argument to mcmcextra, which would allow you to send in Y1-Y3 separately. For now, your best bet is probably to run the modified jags file manually via rjags or runjags. An example of this appears in the blavaan paper at

http://arxiv.org/abs/1511.05604

Also worth mentioning that, even if you could run this via bsem(), I'm not sure that the fitMeasures() command will work. Those metrics depend on the model's marginal log-likelihood, which is computed via lavaan. And when you add extra syntax, it is no longer possible to do that computation in the same way. I plan to add more functionality in the future so that this issue arises less often...

Ed
